scenes.title: Preparing for the coast
scenes.caption: The ships needed food, drinking water and equipment for a coast where supplies could not be guaranteed. At the Indus, loading a fleet meant fitting everyday necessities into vessels that still had to leave room for their crews.

scenes.title: Following the river out
scenes.caption: Before the fleet reached open water, it moved through tidal channels of the Indus. Arrian describes salt water entering with the tide and a passage cut through an obstruction so that the ships could leave at high water.

scenes.title: A short stop on sand
scenes.caption: Krokala was a sandy island where the fleet stopped soon after leaving the river. It was a pause on the way to a more sheltered harbour; the month-long wait for better winds came after this stop.

scenes.title: Thirty-three days in harbour
scenes.caption: Nearchus named the sheltered anchorage Alexander's Haven. Strong winds kept the fleet there for thirty-three days, long enough to fortify the camp while the crews waited for conditions outside the harbour to improve.

scenes.title: Food at the water's edge
scenes.caption: During the long wait, the crews collected shellfish along the shore. Arrian mentions mussels, oysters and unusually large razor-shells: a small part of coastal life that became an important source of food for the stranded fleet.

scenes.title: Ten days of provisions
scenes.caption: At Cocala, the fleet received grain collected under Alexander's orders. Arrian gives the supply as ten days' provisions. The crews also repaired damaged ships before continuing west along a shore with few dependable places to restock.

scenes.title: A contested landing
scenes.caption: The lagoon at the Tomerus offered a place to bring the ships ashore. Local people resisted the landing; Nearchus sent troops against them before the fleet stayed to make repairs. The account records the cost of finding shelter on an inhabited coast.

scenes.title: Rounding Malana
scenes.caption: After the Tomerus, the fleet rounded Malana, the last headland on the Oritan coast in Arrian's account. Cliffs and projecting capes broke the shore into stretches that had to be judged from the water, one passage at a time.

scenes.title: A pilot who knew the coast
scenes.caption: At Mosarna, Hydraces joined the fleet as a local pilot. Arrian says the voyage became easier after his arrival. Knowledge of anchorages, water and coastal conditions mattered as much as the ships or their crews.

scenes.title: Fish laid out to dry
scenes.caption: Fishing supported many communities along the Gedrosian coast. Arrian describes large nets and fish dried in the sun. His broad label for these coastal people hides differences between settlements, some of which also had grain and cultivated land.

scenes.title: Whales ahead of the ships
scenes.caption: Arrian recounts the crews' alarm when they saw whales blowing at sea. Nearchus ordered the ships forward with shouting, trumpets and splashing oars. The animals moved away, leaving the fleet to continue along the coast.

scenes.title: Cultivated ground again
scenes.caption: On reaching Carmania, the fleet encountered a better-watered country. Arrian describes Badis as a settlement with cultivated trees and grain, a welcome change after the difficult supply stops along the Gedrosian coast.

scenes.title: Keeping to the Persian shore
scenes.caption: Beyond Badis, the fleet sighted a headland on the Arabian side of the strait. Onesicritus proposed crossing towards it. Nearchus chose to follow the Persian coast, keeping to the mission of examining its harbours and settlements.

scenes.title: The fleet comes ashore
scenes.caption: At the Anamis, the ships were drawn ashore for repairs. Nearchus left the fleet here while he went inland to find Alexander. The meeting did not end the voyage: he returned to take the ships through the Persian Gulf.

scenes.title: Finding the army inland
scenes.caption: Nearchus and a small party travelled inland from the harbour. Arrian says they were so worn by the voyage that the men sent to find them did not at first recognise them. Their news was that the fleet was safe.

scenes.title: An island and another pilot
scenes.caption: Oaracta had fields, vines and date palms. Its ruler, Mazenes, offered to guide the fleet onward. Leaving the Strait of Hormuz did not remove the need for local knowledge: tides, islands and coastal channels still shaped the passage.

scenes.title: Pearls from the Gulf
scenes.caption: Among the islands off Persis, Nearchus recorded a pearl fishery. For the people living here, the waters were a source of work and trade long before the Macedonian ships arrived. The sketch follows that everyday work at the shore.

scenes.title: Waiting for enough water
scenes.caption: At Gogana, the narrow entrance and shallows made anchoring difficult. A harbour could look close from offshore yet remain hard to enter. The fleet had to work with the tide rather than treat every river mouth as a safe landing.

scenes.title: Gardens on the peninsula
scenes.caption: At Mesambria, Arrian describes a peninsula with gardens and fruit trees. Such places broke up the long stretches of difficult shore. Cultivation depended on water reaching the land, while the fleet still had to find an anchorage nearby.

scenes.title: A channel marked by stakes
scenes.caption: In the Susian shallows, the ships followed stakes marking a narrow passage. Arrian distinguishes this deep, sticky mud from firm sand: a grounded vessel could be difficult to move, even with poles or men trying to push it free.

scenes.title: Cargoes from Arabia
scenes.caption: Diridotis was a trading place for frankincense and other aromatics from Arabia. Here the fleet learned that Alexander was heading towards Susa. Nearchus turned back across the estuary to reach him by the Pasitigris.

scenes.title: Up the Pasitigris
scenes.caption: The fleet left the estuary and travelled up the Pasitigris through inhabited, cultivated country. Nearchus sent messengers ahead to locate Alexander. For the crews, the final approach was a river journey with fields and settlements on either bank.

scenes.title: Ships and army meet
scenes.caption: The fleet reached the bridge where Alexander intended to cross on his way to Susa. Ships moored by the crossing while the sea and land forces came together again. Arrian ends the voyage here, on the Pasitigris.

scenes.title: Flowers for the returning sailors
scenes.caption: Arrian describes sacrifices, games and celebrations when the fleet rejoined the army. Soldiers greeted Nearchus with flowers and ribbons, and Alexander awarded him a gold crown. Months of difficult sailing ended with the crews back among the wider army.
